design_reference: Editeur Livre-Jeu - Wireframes.dc.html § 03 « Mode Outline » variant A (plan indenté du livre) + the « ≣ Outline » switch in the § 02 top bar. Rows = NodeBadge + title, nested by choice edges, relinks marked ↪. Component anatomy + tokens from the design system; low-fi wireframe, light theme.

plan.goal: Show the open book as an indented outline that mirrors the tree, switchable from the canvas, so an author can read and navigate the whole structure as a plan and edit any screen by selecting its row.
acceptance_criteria: The editor top bar exposes a canvas ↔ outline view-mode switch; selecting « Plan » replaces the canvas body with the indented outline and « Arbre » restores the canvas; the node-editor panel stays mounted in both.
The outline lists the book as an indented tree: a depth-first traversal from the sommaire root following choice edges, each row showing the node's badge (kind) + title.
relink / flee edges, convergences, and cycle back-edges render as ↪ reference rows (labelled by edge kind) and are NOT recursed into, so a cyclic book never loops forever.
Nodes unreachable from the root (the isolated mort, free-floating nodes) are listed flat so the whole book is visible.
Clicking a row selects its node through the brain SelectionService; the canvas and node-editor reflect that same selection (single source of truth), and the selected row is highlighted.
A reference row whose target node was deleted is surfaced (⚠ cible supprimée), never crashes the render.
The outline is a live VIEW over BookService (derived inline, no useEffect-synced copy) and holds no private node/edge copy.
The view-mode is a non-synced UI preference (local for the skeleton); it is never written to the book document.
Rows render from design-system tokens/primitives (NodeBadge, tokens), light theme; rows are keyboard-operable with ≥44px targets.
plan.walking_skeleton: buildOutline (pure) flattens the book into indented rows by DFS from the sommaire, following choice edges and emitting reference rows for relink/flee/convergence/cycles/dangling targets, then listing unreachable nodes flat. OutlineView renders the rows (NodeBadge + title), reads the live book via useOpenBook, and selects on click via SelectionService (shared with the canvas, KR-024). The editor shell hoists the shared EditorTopBar with a canvas ↔ outline SegmentedControl and swaps the body.

iterations.goal: Outline fidelity (§ 03 A): hover preview, expand/collapse, per-row rule badges (⊘ prereq, ⏱ countdown) and end-leaf labels; refine reference-row affordance + « centrer dans l'arbre ».
Node inspector (§ 03 B): the node-card summary (entre depuis / victoire / fuite) on row focus, with Éditer + Centrer dans l'arbre actions.
Persist the view-mode + outline expand state via UIPreferencesService (non-synced UI prefs, KR-022) — deferred until that service lands.

known_risks: KR-020 — The outline is a VIEW over BookService; never hold a private node/edge copy. Derive rows inline (useMemo), re-read on node:*/edge:* via useOpenBook.
KR-024 — Selection is the brain SelectionService SSOT; the outline reads via useSelectedNode and writes via selection.select, so canvas + outline + panel never desync.

KR-080 — Outline traversal MUST guard cycles/convergence: a target already shown (or reached by relink/flee) becomes a ↪ reference row, never recursed, so a cyclic book (allowed by design, KR-061) can't infinite-loop; unreachable nodes are listed flat so none are hidden.
KR-021 — A reference/edge whose target node was deleted must be flagged (⚠ cible supprimée), never rendered as a crash or a blank.
KR-022 — The canvas ↔ outline view-mode is a non-synced UI preference, never part of the book document; persistence waits for UIPreferencesService.
KR-068 — Row badges/labels come from the kind registry, not kind tests.
KR-013 — Derive the outline inline/useMemo, not via a useEffect-synced mirror.

iterations_log.label: walking-skeleton
architecture_choices: Hoisted the shared editor chrome out of tree-canvas into brain/components/EditorTopBar (KR-109) and added the canvas ↔ outline SegmentedControl; a new src/EditorScreen shell owns the local view-mode (KR-022) and swaps TreeCanvas ↔ OutlineView while keeping NodeEditorPanel mounted. tree-canvas became the canvas body only.
buildOutline is a pure, view-agnostic DFS (cycle/convergence-safe via a visited set + reference rows, KR-080/061); OutlineView derives rows with useMemo from the live book (KR-020/013).
Selection is shared through the brain SelectionService (KR-024): the outline reads useSelectedNode and writes selection.select, so picking a row reflects on the canvas and the panel.
Row badges/labels read the kind registry (effectiveKind/endLabel/NodeBadge, KR-068); dangling reference targets are flagged ⚠ (KR-021).
deviations_from_plan: View-mode persistence (iteration 3) deferred until UIPreferencesService exists — local state for now, mirroring tree-canvas pan/zoom and book-creation offline-queue deferrals.
Hoisting the top bar to the shell is a tree-canvas change inside this slice, made at the composition seam so both views share one bar (no duplication); CanvasTopBar removed.

test_coverage.unit: buildOutline — nesting, relink reference, choice-cycle guard, isolated-node listing, dangling target, convergence
test_coverage.integration: outline-view via App — view-mode switch shows the outline, row click selects via SelectionService, selection shared across the switch back to the canvas

iterations_log.label: iteration-1
architecture_choices: Expand/collapse lives in a NEW pure helper computeVisibleRows(rows, collapsed) in the same module as buildOutline (KR-080 philosophy: the rule is unit-tested, not discovered in the browser). It walks the flat pre-order rows and hides every later row deeper than a collapsed node until a row at/above its depth resumes — so collapsing hides the exact subtree while later siblings stay. hasChildren is a one-step lookahead; reference rows (↪) are never collapsible (leaves).

Collapsed node ids are LOCAL UI state in OutlineView (a ReadonlySet keyed by node id), derived into visible rows with useMemo — no useEffect-synced mirror (KR-013). The disclosure (▸/▾) is a sibling button of the select button (never nested — button-in-button is invalid), each ≥44px; its aria-label names the node so the collapse target is announced.

Hover preview is a title tooltip built from the node's authored text via the shared brain textLines (KR-068 fallback to a placeholder for an empty screen); the reference row's tooltip instead says « Aller au nœud … » (or « Cible supprimée » for a dangling target, KR-021). End-leaf labels already render through NodeBadge label={endLabel} from the skeleton.

Pre-commit tech-lead review (new workflow: review the uncommitted diff, fix before commit) folded in one nit — rows are keyed by their stable position in the full outline (carried on VisibleOutlineRow.index), not the collapse-filtered index, so toggling a node never remounts the rows below it (no focus loss).
deviations_from_plan: Per-row rule badges (⊘ prereq / ⏱ countdown) deferred: the underlying edge rules (hidden-prerequisite, countdown) do not exist until choice-linking iterations 3–4 — there is nothing to badge yet (same upstream-data deferral as choice-linking iter 1).

« Centrer dans l'arbre » deferred to iteration 2: it needs canvas viewport center-on-node (tree-canvas has no such API yet) plus lifting the view-mode out of EditorScreen, and the spec already lists « Centrer dans l'arbre » in iter 2 alongside the node-inspector's Éditer + Centrer actions — the natural home for the action surface.

test_coverage.unit: computeVisibleRows — hasChildren detection, collapse hides the subtree but keeps siblings, root-collapse hides all, reference rows never collapsible
test_coverage.integration: outline-view via App — collapse/expand hides+restores child rows, screen-text hover preview tooltip, relink reference row with an « Aller au nœud » tooltip

iterations_log.label: iteration-2
architecture_choices: Node inspector summary is a NEW pure helper buildNodeInspector(book, nodeId) (same KR-080 philosophy as buildOutline/computeVisibleRows): it resolves « entre depuis » (every edge whose to === nodeId, carrying the source title + edge kind) and the monstre node's combat outcomes (victoire/fuite targets from node.monster). References resolve by stable id; a deleted source/target surfaces as a null title (KR-021), never a crash. NodeInspector is a dumb presentational card reading that inspection.

The inspected node is LOCAL UI state (inspectedId) set on row focus/hover, falling back to the selection — so the card previews a row WITHOUT committing selection (giving « Éditer » a real job: select the previewed node). Row click still selects (iteration-1 contract preserved). Derived inline, no useEffect mirror (KR-013).

« Centrer dans l'arbre » reveals + centres the node on the canvas. Wired at the COMPOSITION ROOT (EditorScreen owns a {nodeId, seq} RevealRequest): the outline calls an onRevealInTree callback prop; the shell bumps seq + switches viewMode to 'canvas'; TreeCanvas gets the request as a prop and centres once per seq. outline-view and tree-canvas never import each other (same shell-seam as the hoisted top bar). The seq makes repeat reveals distinct; a centred-seq ref means an unrelated re-render (a book edit) never re-centres.

Canvas centering: useViewport gained centerOn(point, size) — pans so a canvas-space point sits at the viewport centre at the current zoom (transform is translate(x,y) scale(zoom), origin 0,0). TreeCanvas reads its surface size from a ref and the node position from resolvePositions, centring on the node's middle (pos + NODE_W/2, NODE_H/2). Runs on mount, so revealing from the outline (which remounts the canvas) lands centred — the EditorScreen-owned prop sidesteps the navigate-then-act timing trap (the event-before-mount problem).
deviations_from_plan: The inspector triggers on row focus/hover (the spec's « on row focus »); it does not also auto-show on plain selection beyond the fallback, to avoid duplicating the always-mounted node-editor panel.

« victoire / fuite » outcomes show only for monstre nodes (the combat outcomes live on node.monster); other kinds show just « entre depuis » since their outgoing structure is already the outline nesting.

test_coverage.unit: buildNodeInspector — incoming links + edge kind + dangling source, monstre victoire/fuite + dangling target, no outcomes for a non-combat node, empty for an unknown id
test_coverage.integration: outline-view via App — focusing a row previews its « entre depuis » in the inspector, Éditer selects a hovered-not-selected node, « Centrer dans l'arbre » switches to the canvas and selects

open_questions: View-mode + expand-state persistence (iteration 3) when UIPreferencesService lands.
« Centrer dans l'arbre » centres but does not yet animate/zoom-to-fit; smooth pan + a zoom-to-node could pair with the iter-3 viewport-persistence work.
